typed-decoding-review.json.scope: Initial phase: read-only typed Beacon SSZ allocation and lifetime audit. Subsequent authorized implementation and checks are recorded separately below. No benchmarks or remote operations.

finding.description: Execution payload root materializes all transaction roots in a temporary Vec before merkle_root, although existing MerkleHasher accepts roots incrementally. This adds exactly 32 bytes per transaction in requested Vec capacity.
finding.bounded_worst_case: The SSZ transaction list permits 1,048,576 elements. Empty inner byte lists are SSZ-decodable with repeated offsets, requiring a 4 MiB offset table and producing 32 MiB temporary transaction roots. This is a shape/allocation example, not an execution-valid block claim.
finding.recommendation: Stream each existing byte_list_root into MerkleHasher::with_leaves(SszTransactions::max_len()), finish, then mix length. This matches pinned ssz_types/src/tree_hash.rs:31-44 and removes linear scratch without introducing a dependency or custom hash algorithm.
tests_proposed: Small empty, one-item and three-item transaction lists, including empty and nonempty byte lists, compared with generic SSZ list roots.
Existing real Fulu block fixed expected root and context controls.
finding.status: Initial review finding; subsequently implemented as recorded below.

dispositions.subject: Variable list decode bounds
dispositions.evidence: ethereum_ssz/src/decode/impls.rs:513-557 sanitizes first offset against actual bytes, requires divisible nonzero four-byte offset table, checks count maximum, then monotonically sanitizes each next offset before slicing. It does not allocate a separate offset vector.

dispositions.subject: Allocation from actual elements
dispositions.evidence: ssz_types/src/variable_list.rs:252-271 caps initial variable-element preallocation at min(iterator upper bound, protocol limit, 131072), then pushes actual decoded elements. Lines284-312 derive fixed-element count from input bytes and reject count over maximum before Vec allocation.

dispositions.subject: No giant tree allocated from type maxima
dispositions.evidence: tree_hash/src/merkle_hasher.rs:168-190 allocates depth-sized accumulator; finish:266-292 completes missing subtrees with cached zero hashes. One-GiB transaction bound controls tree depth, not a one-GiB allocation.

dispositions.subject: Other collection tree roots
dispositions.evidence: ssz_types/src/tree_hash.rs streams basic packed values and composite roots. Other Beacon collections have explicit small protocol limits; no equivalent materialized list-root vector found.

dispositions.subject: Typed lifetime
dispositions.evidence: beacon_block.rs:380-403 keeps SignedBeaconBlockElectraSsz local and returns only Copy VerifiedBeaconBlock metadata. network.rs:3961 and4071 decode sequentially, retaining pairs of compact metadata and raw chunks; typed trees do not accumulate across a response.

limits: Raw RPC reservations are not total allocator/RSS accounting. Typed transaction Vec descriptors, inner byte allocations, and hashing scratch are additional finite temporary memory.

On the current 64-bit target, a Vec descriptor has three machine words; one million inner lists therefore imply approximately 24 MiB descriptor storage, excluding allocator bookkeeping and transient reallocation. This is code-based sizing, not a measured RSS bound.
Typed allocations use ordinary infallible Rust Vec allocation. This review does not establish allocation-failure recovery or a strict process-wide memory ceiling.
CPU work can scale to the protocol element maximum even for empty transactions. No benchmark or execution-transaction semantic validation is claimed.
Only current Electra/Fulu body schema is supported; pre-Electra body support remains unchanged and outside this allocation review.
typed-decoding-review.json.conclusion: No unbounded allocation or escaping typed-tree retention found under existing RPC input limits. Remove the concrete transaction-root scratch allocation; accept and document finite typed decode overhead rather than introduce a new parser/quota architecture without evidence.
